history.summary: Plan r1 committed (8d0176c): six phases (stall alerts corroborated plus a wedge warning with replay-grounded thresholds, Telegram delivery, Keycloak 26.7.3 image and rollout, Grafana and pgAdmin behind client-role-gated clients), the operator pre-run checklist, and 13 acceptance criteria. Two operator questions in plan_questions_r1.md: Q1, how the Keycloak rollout avoids running 26.5.1 beside 26.7.3, which upstream forbids and the chart's surge would do (recommend a permanent stop-before-start rollout; P4 carries it); Q2, the dev-cluster Grafana and pgAdmin copies have no .home hostname, so their redirect addresses are needed (recommend their current MetalLB addresses, supplied by the operator).

Plan r2 committed (2c84db4) with rulings D5, D6 and F3 applied: P4 makes every Keycloak rollout stop the old pod before starting the new one (the Ansible pre-drain hand-off needs no change); P5/P6 put only production's Grafana and pgAdmin behind Keycloak, so the checklist is down to two homelab clients and two secrets and the dev copies keep local login. The push-order health gate no longer relies on the dev cluster, and there are 14 criteria (new V12 for D6), with a stale keycloak-db runbook claim recorded as close-out B3.

Plan is complete against slice.md and its code citations hold, but ruling D2's wedge warning calls the stall alerts 'blind' on a wedged node when they actually fire on the corroborating signal alone (a false critical on srvk8s4 in an ordinary week), and ruling D5 was weighed against a keycloak-db outage that no longer exists — both the operator's to settle.
